apps/model-host.why: PACKAGE.ts runs test/serve.test.mjs and test/transcript.test.mjs, and both bundle src/ with esbuild (build.mjs) and run the bundle, so no resolver reaches the twin (finding E-8). Verifying it needs the build to compile .vibe (vibelang-unplugin), which is cutover work.

apps/app.why: PACKAGE.ts unitTests runs bun over these folders: ~17K tests, 10-18 minutes, too heavy to run twice per iteration on the mini. Both runs use the test files whose relative imports reach a twinned module. Direct importers only while translating (the app entry reaches nearly every test transitively); the full suite runs once on a lane VM before the package counts for cutover.

.smithers/flows.why: The package.json test script runs only test/*.test.ts and test/canary-coding-setup.test.mjs, but the flow folders keep their own suites (issue-sweep/test, release/**, land, quality, issue-claim, docs-sync: node:test; review/tests: bun:test), which PACKAGE.ts targets run (finding E-9). perf/ and bench/ are benchmarks, not suites. land/*.test.* drive the landing flow end to end (more than 150 s, run twice per iteration); they run once before cutover, not per iteration. Both runs skip test/coding-stable-plan.test.ts's 'every coding step flow builds with stable callbacks': it imports every .ts under coding/, which during the twin period includes coding/src-vibe's hatches (they import .vibe files) and .vibe-twin/api-check.ts. It fails because the twins exist, not because of how they behave, and runs once without twins before cutover.

args: --test-skip-pattern=every coding step flow builds with stable callbacks

packages/smithers/build/build-cli.why: Its tests run smthrs builds end to end; the whole suite runs past 10 minutes, twice per iteration. Both runs use the direct importers of twinned modules; the full suite runs once on a lane VM before cutover.

packages/smithers/migrate.why: Its whole suite runs past 18 minutes, twice per iteration. Both runs use the direct importers of twinned modules; the full suite runs once on a lane VM before cutover.

.smithers/flows/coding.why: A package of its own with no tests of its own: .smithers/flows/test exercises it through ../coding imports (E-13). Both runs use those test files.

packages/smithers.why: Its whole Vitest suite runs past 10 minutes, twice per iteration (lane A). Both runs use the direct importers of twinned modules; the full suite runs once on a lane VM before cutover.

packages/smithers/flows/capability.why: test/CapabilityLiterals.test.ts (HARDEN-2) scans the whole repository for capability literals, skipping only node_modules, dist and .git, so it also sees every package's src-vibe twins and .vibe-twin outputs, which copy the TypeScript's literals until cutover. It fails in both runs because of the twins' existence, not their behavior, so both runs exclude it. It runs once, without twins present, before cutover.

packages/smithers/agent/model.why: scripts/provider-live.test.mjs is a node:test file for the provider-live shell guard; PACKAGE.ts runs it as its own NodeTest target. vitest's default include picks it up and fails 'No test suite found' in both runs. It tests a shell script, not Effect code, so both runs exclude it.
